findings.title: Timeline Add to chat silently does nothing for a review-thread comment the host leaves out of the flat comment list
findings.body: The timeline's handler looks the id up only in `detail.comments`, and returns without doing anything when it finds nothing. Timeline thread events come from `pullRequestConversationItems`, which builds the root from `byId.get(comment.id) ?? { ...comment, kind: "review-comment", ... }` (pullRequestDetail.logic.ts:566-575). The comment on line 564-565 says some hosts only include a comment in the thread. On those hosts `event.id` is a thread comment's id that isn't in `detail.comments`. The button still renders, because `event.body` is set, but clicking it adds nothing and shows no toast. `commentTimelineEvent` already puts the resolved comment on `event.comment` (logic.ts:520-523). Pass that comment to the handler, or also search `detail.reviewThreads`, so the click reaches `addCommentToChat`. `addCommentToChat` then finds the thread itself.

findings.title: Deduplicating the pull-request reference by number can skip it for a same-numbered PR from another repository
findings.body: `hasPullRequest` compares only `existing.pullRequest?.number === detail.number`. But `buildPullRequestReferenceContext` keys its chip by URL, and the reason given at pullRequestDetail.logic.ts:1138 is that "repositories can share pull request numbers". Say the composer already holds PR #42 from repository A, and the reader adds a remark from #42 in repository B. The B reference is never added, so B's remark arrives labelled only "PR #42 conversation", with A's title, URL and branches as the only PR context. Comparing `existing.pullRequest?.url` (which is `boundedField(url)`) or the `pr-reference:${url}` id would match the reference's own identity.

findings.title: readableBody returns "" rather than null when an unclosed `<!--` hides all the words
findings.body: `visibleBody` only strips closed comments, so a body like `<!-- bot state` with no `-->` passes the null check on line 670. The loop then drops everything after the unclosed opener and returns `""`, not null. In the comment path this produces a chip whose text is just `octocat:`. In a thread it adds an `author: ` line. The docstring says it returns null for a body with no words. Returning null when `kept.join("\n").trim()` is empty would match it.

findings.title: Resolve loses `ml-auto` when Add to chat is wired but hidden
findings.body: The Add to chat button renders only when `onAddToChat` is set and some comment has a visible body (line 255). Resolve's class, though, tests only `onFix || onAddToChat`. Take a thread with no fix action whose comments are all bookkeeping: neither button that carries `ml-auto` renders, and Resolve sits left-aligned beside the count. Base Resolve's class on the same condition that renders Add to chat.

contracts.action: Add to chat on a timeline conversation or verdict card
contracts.equivalent_path: Summary tab passes the comment object directly via chatSubject (PullRequestSummaryTab.tsx:604,637-639)
contracts.before_after: Summary hands over the comment it rendered. Timeline re-looks the id up in detail.comments only, and silently returns when it is missing.
contracts.visible_effect: On success the detail panel adds the chips and shows the toast 'Added to the composer'. When the lookup misses, nothing happens.
contracts.failure_mode: A thread comment that only appears in reviewThreads (the normalized fallback) isn't found, so the click is a silent no-op.

contracts.action: addCommentToChat writes the PR reference and comment chips into the composer draft
contracts.equivalent_path: ChatComposer's PR reference insertion via buildPullRequestReferenceContext (ChatComposer.tsx:1952, 2607); AnnotatableCodeView addReviewComment (AnnotatableCodeView.tsx:218)
contracts.before_after: Calls are synchronous store writes with no async step. The PR reference is deduplicated by number, while the reference id itself is keyed by URL.
contracts.visible_effect: Chips appear in the composer beside the panel, and a success toast shows.
contracts.failure_mode: No async failure. The handler returns silently when buildPullRequestCommentContext returns null, but the UI hides the button in that case.

contracts.action: Add to chat on a code-tab review thread card
contracts.equivalent_path: Fix button in the same header (line 243-254)
contracts.before_after: Hands over the thread with the loaded comments, mirroring how onFix is wired in PullRequestCodeTab.

summary: Adds an "Add to chat" action to the Summary, Timeline and Code tabs. It attaches a review remark or conversation, plus a reference to the PR, to the composer beside the panel. readableBody strips HTML-comment bookkeeping before the length bound. One fix: the timeline handler looks comments up only in `detail.comments`, so on hosts that keep thread comments only inside reviewThreads, the button silently does nothing. Also suggested: deduplicate the PR reference by URL instead of number, have readableBody return null for an all-hidden body, and fix the Resolve button's alignment when Add to chat is hidden.
